reference_line: The IEC 60364-5-52 correction-factor tables re-typed from published transcriptions of the standard (ambient air B.52.14, ground temperature B.52.15, soil thermal resistivity B.52.16, grouping B.52.17, buried grouping B.52.18, thermal insulation Table 52.2), the Annex G voltage-drop closed form u = b(rho1 L/S cos(phi) + lambda L sin(phi)) I_B, the IEC 60364-4-43 434.5.2 adiabatic equation with the Table 43A k values, the 433.1 I_B <= I_n <= I_z rule and the IEC 60364-5-54 Table 54.2 protective-conductor rule - all implemented independently in python. The raw current-carrying-capacity columns (Table B.52.4 for A1-D2 and B.52.10/B.52.11 for method E) are copyrighted and could not be obtained from any source that reproduces them, so they are treated as an empirical data table: the whole table is read back out of the page and checked for integrity and monotonicity, the one value a public copy of the standard does show (A1, copper, 1,5 mm2 = 13,5 A) is checked exactly, and every copper column is checked against the published two-loaded-conductor Table B.52.2 through a physically bounded ratio. The aluminium columns and the buried D1/D2 columns have no independent source at all and are recorded as flagged, not passed.

IEC 60364-5-52, clause 523.9 and Table 52.2 - cable in a thermally insulating wall: 0,89 / 0,81 / 0,68 / 0,55 for 50 / 100 / 200 / 400 mm, and 0,5 beyond 0,5 m
IEC 60364-4-43:2017, clause 434.5.2 - adiabatic check I^2 t <= k^2 S^2, and Table 43A - k = 115 (Cu/PVC), 143 (Cu/XLPE), 76 (Al/PVC), 94 (Al/XLPE)
IEC 60364-5-54:2011, Table 54.2 - protective conductor cross-section S, 16, S/2
tolerance_line: Agreement to the last digit the page prints: |got-ref| <= 0.5*10^-d + 1e-9*|ref|, with d = 1 decimal for the design current and the corrected ampacity (A), 0 decimals for the ampacity column of the candidate table, 2 decimals for voltage drop (%) and losses (kW), 3 decimals for every correction factor, 1 decimal for the adiabatic minimum section (mm2) and the short-circuit withstand (kA). Every graded quantity is a closed form on both sides, so the only physical slack is double-precision round-off. The ampacity table itself is an empirical data table and is not graded to a numeric tolerance: it is checked for integrity, for one exact primary-source value, and against a 0.82-0.96 (0.78-0.90 for method E) ratio band to the published two-loaded-conductor table with no cell more than 0.06 from its column median.
